backlog.spec: Increase the MAX_ITER constant from 200 to 500 to allow SLSQP more iterations to converge in each attempt.
backlog.title: Increase MAX_ITER

backlog.spec: Modify _solve_once to attempt multiple SLSQP starts from different random initial points until a local optimum is found or time runs out, instead of just one restart.
backlog.title: Multi-start SLSQP with random valid init

backlog.spec: Modify the objective function in _solve_once to include a penalty for being outside the [0, 1] box or for overlaps, rather than relying solely on constraints.
backlog.title: Add Penalty terms to Objective

backlog.spec: Instead of a constant INIT_RADIUS, initialize radii from a distribution (e.g., uniform) scaled to a reasonable average sum.
backlog.title: Variable Radii Initialization

backlog.spec: Implement a greedy approach where circles are added one by one, optimizing the position of the new circle while keeping previous ones fixed.
backlog.title: Sequential Circle Addition

backlog.spec: Explicitly define the box constraints in the minimize call using the 'bounds' parameter instead of just the 'constraints' list.
backlog.title: Coordinate-specific Constraints

backlog.spec: Reduce the SHRINK constant to a smaller value (e.g., 1e-12) to allow for tighter packings.
backlog.title: Dynamic SHRINK constant

backlog.spec: Modify _repair to iteratively project the centers to be valid (within the box) and then shrink radii until overlaps are removed.
backlog.title: Improved Repair: Iterative Projection

backlog.spec: Initialize radii such that their sum is close to the target 2.63, providing a better starting point for the optimizer.
backlog.title: Scaled Radius Initialization

backlog.spec: In _repair, instead of just shrinking the two overlapping circles, shrink all circles involved in a cluster of overlaps.
backlog.title: Soft-min Repair

backlog.spec: Use the gradient of the overlap distance to move centers during the repair step, rather than just shrinking radii.
backlog.title: Gradient-based Repair

backlog.spec: Calculate the remaining time more accurately inside the loop to ensure the script doesn't exceed the 45s hard limit.
backlog.title: Adaptive Time Limit

backlog.spec: After SLSQP, run a short Simulated Annealing step to nudge circles and expand radii.
backlog.title: Simulated Annealing Post-Processing

backlog.spec: Use the L-BFGS-B method instead of SLSQP, which handles box constraints natively and is often faster.
backlog.title: L-BFGS-B for Box Constraints

backlog.spec: Use a quasi-random sequence (like Sobol) to initialize circle centers to cover the space more uniformly.
backlog.title: Sobol Sequence Initialization

backlog.spec: Sort radii in descending order during initialization to place larger circles in more 'stable' positions first.
backlog.title: Pre-sorted Radii

backlog.spec: Introduce a weight parameter for the overlap constraints in the objective function to balance the 'sum of radii' goal.
backlog.title: Overlap Penalty Weight

backlog.spec: In the constraints function, use r_i <= c_x_i <= 1-r_i and r_i <= c_y_i <= 1-r_i as distinct constraints.
backlog.title: Better Box Constraint Formulation

backlog.spec: In _repair, give circles a 'velocity' based on the direction of overlap and move them slightly.
backlog.title: Velocity-based Repair

backlog.spec: Apply the repair step recursively until all overlaps are gone, using a smaller shrink factor in each recursion.
backlog.title: Recursive Repair

backlog.spec: Replace SLSQP with a simple SGD step that updates centers and radii based on the gradient of the sum of radii plus overlap penalties.
backlog.title: Stochastic Gradient Descent

backlog.spec: Since multi-threading is not available, use a 'multi-start' logic that runs 5 quick optimizations instead of 1 long one.
backlog.title: Multi-threading (Pseudo)

backlog.spec: Initialize centers using a hexagonal grid pattern and then let the optimizer perturb them.
backlog.title: Initial Packing via Hexagonal Grid

backlog.spec: Optimize the distance calculation in the constraints function by using squared distances to avoid unnecessary sqrt calls.
backlog.title: Circle-Circle Distance Check

backlog.spec: Make the SHRINK amount proportional to the magnitude of the overlap.
backlog.title: Shrink factor scaling

backlog.spec: Add a constraint or a penalty to ensure no single radius becomes excessively large at the expense of others.
backlog.title: Max Radius Cap

backlog.spec: Fix the positions of the largest circles and only optimize the positions/radii of the smaller ones.
backlog.title: Sequential Optimization

backlog.spec: Reduce the INIT_LOW value to 0.01 to allow circles to start closer to the boundaries.
backlog.title: Tighter Init Bounds

backlog.spec: Use a Newton-Raphson step to resolve overlaps by solving the system of equations for minimal radius reduction.
backlog.title: Newton-Raphson Repair

backlog.spec: After each SLSQP run, slightly perturb the radii and rerun for a few iterations to escape local minima.
backlog.title: Randomized Radius Perturbation

backlog.spec: Instead of optimizing all 26 circles simultaneously from scratch, add circles one by one. For each new circle, solve for its optimal center and radius given the current fixed positions of the previous circles (using SLSQP or a simple local search), then proceed to the next. This ensures each circle is 'nestled' into the current best packing.
backlog.title: Sequential Circle Addition

backlog.spec: Refactor the problem to use L-BFGS-B by treating the boundary constraints (0 <= x <= 1, 0 <= y <= 1) as simple box bounds. To handle the non-overlap constraints, move them into a penalty term in the objective function (e.g., Objective = -sum(radii) + lambda * sum(max(0, overlap_dist))). This allows using a more efficient second-order optimizer than SLSQP.
backlog.title: L-BFGS-B for Box Constraints

backlog.spec: Instead of uniform random initialization, generate a hexagonal grid of circles across the unit square. Randomly jitter the positions and radii of these grid circles to create the starting point for the SLSQP solver. A hexagonal packing is the densest 2D packing, providing a much better basin of attraction than random noise.
backlog.title: Initial Packing via Hexagonal Grid

backlog.spec: Modify the objective function to include a heavy penalty for overlaps: Objective = -sum(radii) + Ω * ∑ max(0, r_i + r_j - dist_{ij})^2. Use a very high Ω (e.g., 1e6). Start with a lower Ω and gradually increase it (continuation method) to guide the solver toward a feasible, high-density region.
backlog.title: Overlap Penalty Weight

backlog.spec: Instead of allowing radii to be any value from INIT_RADIUS to 1.0, calculate a maximum possible radius (e.g., 0.3 or 0.4) based on the area of the unit square. Better yet, use a distribution for radii (like a power-law or weighted random) so that fewer large circles and many small circles are attempted, which is often more efficient for packing.
backlog.title: Tighter Init Bounds

backlog.spec: Enhance the repair step to be recursive. When an overlap is detected between circle i and j, identify the 'neighborhood' of circles that are also involved in overlaps with i or j. Solve a local sub-problem to shift/shrink the entire neighborhood simultaneously to resolve all local overlaps in one step, rather than fixing only one pair at a time.
backlog.title: Recursive Repair

backlog.spec: Monitor the progress of the SLSQP solver. If the solver is making slow progress (small change in objective per iteration), terminate it early and restart with a new random seed. Conversely, if it is converging rapidly, allow it to run longer. This ensures the 30s budget is spent on promising regions.
backlog.title: Adaptive Time Limit

backlog.spec: Sort the radii in descending order before starting the optimization. By placing larger circles first or giving them higher priority in the objective/constraints, the solver is forced to find positions for the 'hard' constraints first, making the refinement of smaller circles much easier.
backlog.title: Pre-sorted Radii

backlog.spec: Replace the iterative shrink repair with a Newton-Raphson step. Calculate the gradient and Hessian of the overlap distances. When an overlap occurs, take a step in the direction that minimizes the overlap while maximizing the radii, using a line search to ensure the step doesn't make the packing worse.
backlog.title: Newton-Raphson Repair

backlog.spec: Incorporate a soft penalty or a hard constraint that prevents any single radius from exceeding a certain threshold (e.g., 0.4). This prevents the solver from wasting time trying to fit a single massive circle that effectively blocks large portions of the square, favoring a more distributed and eventually denser packing.
backlog.title: Max Radius Cap

backlog.spec: After the L-BFGS-B optimization, take the best result and run a short simulated annealing (SA) phase. In each SA step, randomly perturb the centers of the circles by a small amount and adjust the radii slightly to maintain validity. Use a cooling schedule to gradually reduce the perturbation magnitude. This helps escape local optima found by the gradient-based solver.
backlog.title: Simulated Annealing Post-Processing

backlog.spec: Instead of optimizing all 26 circles simultaneously, place them one by one. For each circle, find the best location and radius that doesn't overlap with the already placed circles. Once all are placed, perform a global optimization step (the current L-BFGS-B routine) to allow them to 'settle' and expand into the gaps.
backlog.title: Sequential Circle Addition

backlog.spec: Modify the repair step so that the shrink factor is not constant. Calculate the magnitude of the overlap for each pair; pairs with larger overlaps should be shrunk more aggressively than pairs with minor overlaps. This prevents large overlaps from dominating the repair process and allows smaller overlaps to be handled more gently.
backlog.title: Dynamic Shrink Factor

backlog.spec: Instead of uniform initialization across [0, 1], use a heuristic to initialize circles. For example, place larger circles first in a quasi-random pattern and smaller circles in the remaining space. Alternatively, initialize all radii to a very small common value (e.g., 0.02) and centers to a jittered grid, then let the solver expand them.
backlog.title: Tighter Init Bounds

backlog.spec: In the objective function, introduce a small penalty for circles being too close to the boundary unless they are small. This encourages circles to 'push' against each other to create more efficient packing structures, as the current penalty might let them float freely near walls.
backlog.title: Coordinate-specific Constraints

backlog.spec: Instead of starting from an invalid packing and repairing it, generate initial packings that are guaranteed to be valid (e.g., by placing tiny circles one by one in available space). Then, run the L-BFGS-B optimizer starting from these valid configurations. This ensures the solver always starts in a feasible region of the search space.
backlog.title: Multi-start with Random Valid Init

backlog.spec: Add a regularization term or a constraint that limits the maximum radius of any single circle to a reasonable upper bound (e.g., 0.25). This can prevent the solver from creating one massive circle and 25 tiny ones, which might be a local optimum, and instead encourage a more balanced distribution of sizes.
backlog.title: Max Radius Cap

backlog.spec: Implement a dynamic time allocation. If the first few restarts of `_solve_once` are yielding very poor results (low radius sum), increase the `MAX_ITER` or the time spent per restart. If the solver finds a very good result quickly, spend more time on 'polishing' that specific result using a high-precision local search.
backlog.title: Adaptive Time Limit

backlog.spec: Replace the linear shrinking repair with a Newton-Raphson-based approach. For any overlapping circles, treat the overlap as a differentiable constraint violation and use the gradient of the distance function to 'push' the centers apart and shrink the radii simultaneously until the overlap is zero.
backlog.title: Newton-Raphson Repair

backlog.spec: After completing the L-BFGS-B penalty continuation, perform a local search by taking the best found packing and applying a small random perturbation to the centers/radii, then running a few iterations of L-BFGS-B without the penalty weights to 'settle' into the nearest local optimum. This helps escape saddle points or local optima found by the penalty method.
backlog.title: Basin-Hopping style local search

backlog.spec: Implement an architecture where centers and radii are optimized in alternating stages. First, optimize the radii given fixed centers (solving a simple linear program or a simpler L-BFGS-B call), then optimize the centers given those radii. Repeat this for a fixed number of cycles before the final penalty continuation.
backlog.title: Multi-level Coordinate Descent

backlog.spec: Replace the random initialization with a greedy sequential placement: place circles one by one at the 'best' available position (highest available area/distance from others) with a small amount of added noise. Use the resulting packing as the starting point for the L-BFGS-B penalty continuation.
backlog.title: Greedy Sequential Packing with Noise

backlog.spec: Add a specialized final polish step that specifically targets the most violated constraints. Calculate the maximum overlap $\Delta_{ij} = r_i + r_j - d_{ij}$. For each overlapping pair, reduce both radii by $\Delta_{ij}/2$ iteratively until no overlaps remain. Perform this multiple times (e.g., 100 iterations) to ensure a strictly valid packing for the harness.
backlog.title: Shrink-to-Fit Exact Polish

backlog.spec: Dynamically adjust the penalty weight continuation schedule based on the elapsed time. If the solver is running out of time, skip the lower weight stages (10.0, 1e2) and jump straight to high-penalty stages (1e4, 1e5) to ensure the solver converges to a feasible point within the 30s limit.
backlog.title: Time-Proportional Penalty Schedules

backlog.spec: Instead of a fixed INIT_RADIUS, initialize radii using a distribution where larger circles are prioritized but with high variance. Since the goal is the sum of radii, having a few very large circles (occupying the corners/edges) and many small ones (filling gaps) is often better than uniform sizes.
backlog.title: Entropy-based Radius Initialization

backlog.spec: Instead of a fixed schedule (10 to 1e5), use an adaptive schedule where the penalty weight $\lambda$ increases based on the magnitude of the current violation $\sum p^2$. Specifically, set $\lambda = \max(1e1, \frac{\text{target-error}}{\sum p^2})$.
backlog.title: Adaptive Penalty Weighting

backlog.spec: Implement a physics-based relaxation: treat overlaps as repulsive forces. For each circle $i$ overlapping with $j$, calculate a force vector directed away from the center of $j$. Update centers $c_i$ based on the sum of forces over a fixed number of steps. This can be used as a pre-processing step to 'untangle' initial layouts.
backlog.title: Force-Directed Relaxation

backlog.spec: Modify the objective function to include a heavy 'barrier' penalty for circles approaching the walls (e.g., a $1/(r - (1-x))^2$ type term). This prevents circles from 'jittering' against the boundaries and allows L-BFGS-B to find better packing configurations near the edges.
backlog.title: Hard-Boundary Penalty

backlog.spec: Approximate the overlap constraints as linear constraints by linearizing the distance formula $d_{ij}$ around the current coordinates $c_{ij}$. Solve the resulting convex problem (or a quadratic approximation) to update $c$ and $r$, and repeat. This is a more stable alternative to the pure penalty method.
backlog.title: Successive Convex Approximation

backlog.spec: After the L-BFGS-B optimization and repair, run a fixed number of iterations of coordinate descent. In each iteration, cycle through each circle and update its center (x, y) to the optimal position for that fixed radius, considering only the constraints of other circles and the unit square boundaries (projecting the center onto the feasible region).
backlog.title: Coordinate Descent Polish

backlog.spec: Instead of a fixed schedule of penalty weights (10.0 to 1e5), use a dynamic schedule where the penalty weight $\lambda$ is proportional to the remaining time in the 30s budget. Start with a lower weight and ramp up exponentially to a very high value as the time limit approaches, ensuring the solver works harder on 'tightening' the packing in the final seconds.
backlog.title: Time-Proportional Penalty Scaling

backlog.spec: Replace the random center initialization with a greedy sequential placement: place circles one by one, each at the point that allows for the largest possible radius without overlapping existing circles. After placing all 26, use the L-BFGS-B optimizer to 'expand' the circles and shift their centers simultaneously.
backlog.title: Greedy Sequential with Noise and Polish

backlog.spec: Add a specific penalty term to the objective function that penalizes circles for being closer than $1e-7$ to the boundary (e.g., $\sum \max(0, r - x)^2 + \sum \max(0, r - (1-x))^2$). This creates a 'buffer zone' that prevents the optimizer from pushing circles into 'sticky' boundary states where gradients become numerically unstable.
backlog.title: Hard-Boundary Penalty Term

backlog.spec: Implement a force-directed relaxation where each overlapping circle $i$ experiences a repulsive force from any circle $j$ that it overlaps with. The force magnitude is proportional to the depth of the overlap. Move centers along the vector $c_i - c_j$ for a small number of steps to 'untangle' the packing before the final L-BFGS-B pass.
backlog.title: Voronoi-based Force Push

backlog.spec: Implement a nested optimization: the 'outer' loop optimizes the radii $r$ using a gradient-based approach, while the 'inner' loop optimizes the centers $c$ for those fixed radii using coordinate descent. Repeat this alternating cycle for a set number of times to find a local maximum.
backlog.title: Multi-level Coordinate Descent

backlog.spec: Replace the current `_repair` function with a more robust iterative projection. In each step, for every circle that violates a boundary or overlaps another, project its center to the nearest point that satisfies the constraint, and if the center cannot be moved without causing new overlaps, shrink its radius by a factor $\alpha = 1 - \text{overlap}/(	ext{sum of radii})$.
backlog.title: Shrink-to-Fit Exact Polish

backlog.spec: Generate a hexagonal lattice of points that fits within the unit square. Select $n$ points from this lattice, then apply a small random displacement (jitter) to each. Initialize the radii such that they are as large as possible without overlap (using a Voronoi-based approach or simple sequential growth), then start the L-BFGS-B optimization.
backlog.title: Jittered Hexagonal Voronoi Start

backlog.spec: Instead of just large radii, initialize radii $r_i$ such that $\sum r_i$ is maximized subject to $\sum r_i^2 < C$ for some constant $C$. This prevents the optimizer from starting with a single massive circle and 25 tiny ones, encouraging a more balanced 'packed' distribution from the start.
backlog.title: Entropy-based Radius Initialization (Modified)

backlog.spec: Modify the penalty continuation so that $\lambda$ increases based on the *gradient* of the violation. If the total violation is decreasing slowly, increase $\lambda$ more aggressively. If the violation is large but the gradient is small (stuck in a local minimum), apply a small random 'kick' to the centers before continuing with the penalty schedule.
backlog.title: Adaptive Penalty Weighting

backlog.spec: In each restart, instead of purely relying on L-BFGS-B, incorporate a simulated annealing phase where centers are perturbed slightly and radii are updated. Use a decreasing temperature schedule to 'shake' the circles out of local configurations before the final L-BFGS-B penalty optimization. This helps explore the configuration space more broadly than a local gradient descent.
backlog.title: Simulated Annealing for Global Search

backlog.spec: Instead of random initial centers, implement a greedy sequential placement: sort radii in descending order and place each circle at the first available position (found via a coarse grid) that doesn't overlap with existing circles. Then, run L-BFGS-B from this 'packed' starting point to maximize the radii while maintaining non-overlap.
backlog.title: Greedy Packing with Randomized Radius Order

backlog.spec: Modify the penalty schedule to have distinct phases. First, use very low weights (10-100) to allow the circles to move freely into an 'unpacked' state; then, use a geometric progression (e.g., 10^2, 10^3, 10^4, 10^5, 10^6, 10^7) to slowly 'harden' the constraints. This is designed to prevent the solver from getting stuck in high-penalty-gradient regions early on.
backlog.title: Multi-Phase Penalty Continuation

backlog.spec: During the L-BFGS-B optimization, every 50 iterations, temporarily drop the penalty weight $\lambda$ by 50% for 10 iterations before returning to the current weight. This 'tunneling' effect allows the solver to jump over high-energy barriers in the penalty landscape that might be trapping the current configuration.
backlog.title: Intermittent Penalty Relaxation

backlog.spec: Before the L-BFGS-B step, apply a force-directed relaxation where every circle exerts a repulsive force on its neighbors. The force magnitude should be proportional to the depth of the overlap. Run this for a fixed number of iterations (e.g., 100) to reach a 'relaxed' state before starting the formal gradient optimization.
backlog.title: Voronoi-based Repulsion Force

backlog.spec: Instead of optimizing radii directly as independent variables, optimize a set of 'potential radii' $p_i$. Let the actual radius $r_i$ be calculated as $r_i = 	ext{min}(p_i, 	ext{local constraints})$. This ensures that the optimization objective (maximizing $\sum r_i$) is always consistent with the physical constraints of the unit square.
backlog.title: Dynamic Radius Scaling

backlog.spec: Manually scale the step size of the L-BFGS-B update based on the gradient of the penalty term. If the penalty $\sum p^2$ increases significantly in a single step, reduce the step size; if it decreases or remains stable, allow the solver to take larger steps. This mimics a learning rate scheduler for the second-order optimizer.
backlog.title: Adaptive Learning Rate for L-BFGS-B

backlog.spec: Instead of calculating all $O(n^2)$ pairwise overlaps in every gradient step, maintain a spatial hash grid or a neighbor list. Only calculate penalties for circles in the same or adjacent cells. This speeds up the gradient calculation significantly, allowing for more iterations or more complex penalty schedules within the time limit.
backlog.title: N-body Constraint Approximation

backlog.spec:
Replace the current repair step with a SOR-inspired approach: iteratively project circles to be non-overlapping with their neighbors. In each iteration, move the circle slightly further than the projection distance (relaxation factor $\omega 
eq 1$) to accelerate convergence and prevent oscillations in dense areas.
backlog.title: Successive Over-Relaxation (SOR) Repair

backlog.spec: After each L-BFGS-B convergence, if the packing is valid, apply a small random perturbation to the radii (e.g., $r_i 	o r_i + \epsilon$ where $\epsilon$ is small and random) and perform one quick 'polishing' L-BFGS-B pass. This helps the solver escape local maxima by slightly 'growing' the packing and re-adjusting.
backlog.title: Entropy-based Radius Perturbation

incumbent.description: Replace the SLSQP local solver with L-BFGS-B over box-bounded centres and radii, using an analytic gradient and an increasing quadratic penalty for overlap and wall violations, then keep the existing repair step.

memo:
Helped: only the optimizer swap in slot 10 (SLSQP to L-BFGS-B with penalty continuation). It scored -2.6315 and -2.6327, delta -0.0041. The incumbent is -2.6321 over 2 runs, and about 0.004 remains to the published 2.6360.

Did not help: repair-step variants, which were mostly aborted. Also MAX_ITER 500, early stopping, annealing, the quadratic penalty, Sobol starts, penalty weight 1e6, Pareto radii, radius perturbation, OVERLAP_W=3, final polish, basin hopping, adaptive penalty schedules. Most sit within noise (sd about 0.0023) of the incumbent. Several early slots show an identical -2.6261, so check that those edits really change the output.

Promising: structured starts under L-BFGS-B. Jittered hex scored -2.6340, and a second hex variant scored -2.6359 and -2.6321 (delta -0.0019). Greedy centres scored -2.6344 and -2.6354 (delta -0.0028, 2 runs). Jittered grid scored -2.6338.

Next: adopt the greedy-centre start, which is best and replicated. Then combine it with hex or grid starts, and tune the penalty schedule. Replicate before accepting anything.
